releasePreviews.title: ESPHome 2026.11.0: Lighter builds and tougher updates
releasePreviews.body:
ESPHome 2026.11.0: Lighter builds and tougher updates

Nov 18, 2026
Jesse Hills
ESPHome Developer

NOTE

This is a beta release. Details on this page may change before the stable release is published.

ESPHome publishes a release like this each month, so you can see what’s new, what’s fixed and anything to be aware of before you update.

Short on time? Here’s the quick version
Section titled “Short on time? Here’s the quick version”

This is the short, plain-language version for anyone short on time or still finding their way around ESPHome. The full technical post continues below.

Sub-devices: every entry under esphome: devices: now needs a relation: field – via for a separate physical device reached through this node, child for a logical part of this node.

HTTP requests in scripts: http_request.get,.post and.send no longer pause the script, so add mode: queued or mode: parallel where repeated runs must not be skipped.

ESP-IDF minimum version: if your ESP32 build pins the ESP-IDF framework to a 5.0 version, move it to 5.1 or newer (or remove the pin).

Power meters on Beken chips: on BK72xx, hlw8012 power meters with short pulses, such as the BL0937, on inverted
pins previously double counted each pulse. They now count each pulse once and match ESP32, so if a plug calibrated on
an older release reads half after updating, double voltage_divider and the current calibration (see the checklist
below).

New features: ESPHome uses less memory on every supported chip, especially the ESP8266, and the way automations are built now produces smaller, faster code.

Also in this release: over thirty new components plus many smaller fixes and improvements.

If you’re running a typical config, there’s nothing else you need to check before updating – aside from the items above and a few rarer setups covered in the upgrade checklist.

For the full release overview and technical detail – including anything that affects custom lambdas, external components or non-standard setups – keep reading below.

Release overview
Section titled “Release overview”

ESPHome 2026.11.0 is a framework release. Another large sweep of entity names, filter tables and lookup strings leaves
RAM on ESP8266 and lives in flash on every platform. Scheduler timers lose their string names, cover, fan, valve and
lock traits pack into one byte, and several components switch from heap vectors to fixed buffers. The generated code
for automations now compiles to plain C++ control flow, saving about 1.6 KB of RAM on ESP8266 and ESP32 IDF for a modest
configuration.

Codegen gets a wave of shared helpers, so new components and migrations need less boilerplate: new Apply entity
classes for hub-forwarding buttons, switches, numbers and selects, SUB_* and PUBLISH_STATE macros for child
entities, and byte, I2C, UART, BLE and modbus helpers that roll out across dozens of drivers. The minimum ESP-IDF rises
to 5.1, LibreTiny goes to 1.14.0 with BDK 3.0.78 on Beken chips, and esp_hosted moves to 3.1.0. Native ESPHome OTA
now falls back to UDP when the link is lossy, so uploads finish on Wi-Fi that would stall the previous TCP data phase.
wifi: ap: with web_server: now serves the interface as a captive portal, the DHCP lease is cached across reboots
and Wi-Fi Easy Connect lands on ESP32.

OpenThread on ESP32 gains an experimental border router that bridges Thread to Wi-Fi. nRF52 picks up a crash coredump,
a native toolchain entry, a dongle board, BLE OTA through the Adafruit bootloader and SMP-over-UDP. HTTP requests from
automations no longer block the main loop, the logger buffers early boot lines for later replay over the API, and the
web server stops exposing internal entities over REST. This release also adds over thirty new components, including
Daikin Madoka BLE, USB audio and keyboard, an RTSP server, a VNC client, BLE MIDI, HDMI-CEC and the ESP32 ULP
coprocessor, twelve new climate IR platforms, and many new sensors, radars and expanders. A short codebase-correctness
sweep closes memory, event-decoding and REST-visibility bugs.

Fixes made during the beta make Wi-Fi reconnects, MQTT and Bluetooth proxies more reliable. They also stop several
watchdog resets on ESP8266 and timing errors on Realtek chips.

Upgrade checklist
Section titled “Upgrade checklist”

If you use esphome: devices: for sub-devices, add relation: via (separate physical device) or relation: child
(logical part of this node) to every entry.

If you use OpenThread on ESP32, make sure your build uses ESP-IDF 5.5.5 or newer; remove any pinned
esp32.framework.version older than that.

If you target the ESP32 with ESP-IDF, remove any pin to ESP-IDF 5.0.x; the minimum is now 5.1.

If you use esp32_hosted, require ESP-IDF 5.5 or newer, add d1_pin on a 1-bit SDIO setup, and remove
active_high: false (use the default; active_high: true works with a deprecation warning).

If you use OpenThread on ESP32 without anything else that needs IPv4, add network: enable_ipv4: true to keep
IPv4 on.

If you use http_request actions inside a script, set mode: queued or mode: parallel where repeated runs must
not be skipped; actions no longer block the script.

If you have clk_mode: on the ethernet: component, move it to the clk: block with mode: and pin:.

If you have provider: on dlms_meter:, drop it; for provider: netznoe add the two custom_patterns from the
release notes.

If you have DLMS meter sensors using predefined keys such as voltage_l1 or timestamp, replace each with its
own entity using obis_code.

If you have update_on_release: on an LVGL number, replace it with trigger: on_release.

If you have dump_device_info: on nextion:, delete it; device info is always logged.

If you have platform: qspi_amoled, change it to platform: qspi_dbi.

If you use delay, wait_until or script.wait inside emonTx on_json / on_data, MQTT on_json_message, or
Haier on_status_message, copy the values you need into globals first and defer from a separate script.

If you drive internal entities through the web server REST API by URL, add include_internal: true under
web_server:.

If you have NEC remote_transmitter.transmit_nec actions with command_repeats above 10 or equal to 0, change
them to a value between 1 and 10.

If you have on_nec lambdas comparing x.command_repeats, update them - the value is always 1 now and the check
no longer works.

If you have Panasonic IR configs captured from a 56-bit remote, run the dumper again and update address_2 and
command.

If you have MagiQuest on_magiquest lambdas comparing x.wand_id or x.magnitude, re-dump and use the new values.

If you have a canbus.send with a constant payload longer than 8 bytes, shorten it to at most 8 bytes.

If you use esp32_rmt_led_strip, remote_transmitter or remote_receiver with a custom rmt_symbols or multiple
components, re-run validation; conflicts and invalid sizes now fail at config time.

If you use color_bwr e-paper panels (WeAct 3C, Waveshare B, Waveshare BWR, Inkplate 2), expect color mapping to
change; the test card and lambdas on WeAct 3C or Waveshare 7.5” V2 BWR also change because they now report
DISPLAY_TYPE_COLOR.

If you use the CB3S board (LN-CB3S V1.0) with the D12 alias, update your pin to D13 or PA11; D12 now
drives PA10.

If you use hlw8012 (HLW8012, BL0937, CSE7759) on a BK72xx (Beken) chip with inverted pins and the readings dropped
to half after updating (typical for the BL0937, whose pulses are 38 µs), update the calibration: pulses of about 50 µs
or less were previously double counted on Beken chips, and each pulse is now counted once, the same as on ESP32. To
keep your calibration, double voltage_divider (this also corrects power and energy) and double the current: double
an existing multiply filter on the current sensor, or add multiply: 2. Leave current_resistor as it is, because
power depends on both values and halving it as well would double power a second time. Then check the readings against
a known load. With pins that are not inverted, these short pulses were missed before and are now counted; pulses
between about 75 and 150 µs were miscounted either way. The same applies to pulse_counter with
internal_filter: 0us; with the default filter, and for slower pulses such as water and gas meters, pulse_counter
on Beken chips counts as before ( #21271 ).

If you use hlw8012 (HLW8012, BL0937, CSE7759) on a Realtek chip, check its calibration: on RTL8720C it counted no
pulses at all on older releases, and on RTL8710B it counted nothing with inverted pins; both now read correctly, the
same as on ESP32. pulse_counter with internal_filter: 0us counts there too; with the default filter it still
counts nothing on RTL8720C, or with inverted pins on RTL8710B
( #21271 ). LN882H reads the pin within a few microseconds of a pulse
edge, so it counted these pulses correctly before and needs no change.

If a browser page on another site calls web OTA /update, Prometheus /metrics, the index page or the ESP32
/events stream, add that site to web_server: allowed_origins:. Each entry can be at most 127 characters.

If you use deep_sleep with wakeup_pin on an ESP32-H2, replace it with esp32_ext1_wakeup using the same pin.

If your device receives MQTT messages over 8 KB (ESP8266), 16 KB (LibreTiny) or 32 KB (ESP32), raise the new
max_payload_size option under mqtt:. Larger messages are now dropped with a warning.

ESP8266 RAM diet and framework-wide flash tables
Section titled “ESP8266 RAM diet and framework-wide flash tables”

ESP8266 keeps on a strict RAM budget, and this release shaves another large chunk off it by moving constant tables and
strings into flash. Entity names, device classes, icons, log tags, filter tables, effect lists, enum option lookups
and action payloads now live in flash on every build, and are only copied into RAM when a component actua…

articles.title: More room for automations and fewer stalled updates
articles.dek: ESPHome 2026.11 arrives today; sub-devices and scripts that fetch web data need a configuration check.
body: Small ESP8266 boards have little working memory to spare. The release keeps more fixed names and lookup tables in flash storage instead, and builds automation steps into smaller programs. In the official example, eight three-step automations use about 1.6 KB less working memory on ESP8266 and on ESP32 builds using Espressif’s development framework.

Wireless firmware uploads gain another way through a poor connection: the transfer can switch methods when Wi-Fi is losing packets, avoiding stalls in the previous upload path. Devices can also retain early startup messages and replay them after a client connects, making faults from before Wi-Fi was ready easier to investigate.

New components broaden what makers can connect. Compatible ESP32 boards can capture from USB microphones and play through USB sound cards, while an ESP32 camera can supply a stream understood by players such as VLC and surveillance software such as Frigate. The release also includes an experimental way to bridge a Thread device network to Wi-Fi.

Before updating, check configurations that describe sub-devices: each needs a relation field identifying a separate physical device or a logical part of the same node. Scripts making web requests need queued or parallel mode when repeated runs must not be skipped. Builds pinned to version 5.0 of Espressif’s development framework need at least 5.1. Owners of affected Beken smart plugs whose power readings halve should follow the release notes’ recalibration instructions and check against a known load.

articles.title: Watch what is happening during startup
articles.dek: A live details panel counts completed integrations, identifies failures and keeps a summary after the system finishes.
body: An integration taking a long time to start no longer hides what the others are doing. The startup message opens a live view of the current phase, the connections still being set up and how long each has been running.

Completion appears when the system is actually running, with a warning if any integrations need attention. The summary retains the total startup time and the slowest integrations; familiar icons help identify them, with a separate alert beside failures.
Erwin Douna connects the new screen to the startup reporting added earlier this month. It explains the wait without changing how integrations are scheduled or how long they are allowed to take.

articles.title: Stereo pairs and home theaters take one place in the player list
articles.dek: Changes made in the Sonos app follow through, and speakers removed from a set return with fresh settings.
body: A surround speaker that belongs to a soundbar should not remain in the player list as an unusable separate destination. The server removes those obsolete Sonos entries and their settings, while showing the complete set with its speaker layout, such as stereo or 5.1.

Chromecast speaker pairs use the same multi-channel category. These sets behave like one speaker when playing music or joining a group, and their own volume counts toward the group level when they lead it. A filter in the player list helps find them.
The Sonos layout follows changes made in the manufacturer’s app. Taking a speaker out of a pair or theater set brings it back as a new player; this does not create or configure the set itself.

articles.title: Let the battery report its usable capacity
articles.dek: Manual entry remains available, while changing measurements feed the combined charge percentage.
body: If a storage system already measures how much energy it can hold, its reading can replace a fixed number in the Energy settings. The combined battery charge percentage follows that usable capacity as it changes, giving larger batteries the appropriate weight.

The selector accepts capacity in watt-hours, kilowatt-hours or megawatt-hours. A missing or invalid reading falls back to the existing calculation for batteries without a capacity; the field is for usable capacity, not remaining energy or lifetime production.
Thomas van Tilburg’s first contributions to Home Assistant Core and the frontend bring the setting and its calculation together. Existing configurations keep their manual capacity values.

articles.title: Turn a radio discovery into a saved song
articles.dek: The web player separates track actions from station actions; an installed recognition provider can fill gaps in programme information.
body: Hear something worth keeping while a station is playing? The heart menu in the player bar and full-screen web player puts the named song first, with options to save it to favorites or a playlist. The station has its own entries beneath it.

The search through your music services happens only when you choose an action. If the song cannot be found, the player explains that and leaves the library unchanged. Talk, adverts and stations without an identified song retain the station menu.

An installed music-recognition provider can also supply the title and artist when a station sends none. Those details appear as playback reaches the recognized audio; the station’s own information takes priority, and recognition results are not stored.

articles.title: Weather warnings show the highest level in effect
articles.dek: Future Portuguese alerts no longer appear as though they have already begun.
body: A yellow warning could hide an orange one simply because it appeared first in the district’s response. The Weather Alert sensor instead selects the most severe warning whose start and end times include the present moment, and shows its details.

@JorgeS15’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core also makes the state unknown when warnings cannot be retrieved. The correction avoids treating an alert published days ahead as a current condition.

articles.title: Room and hot-water settings reach Aerosmart
articles.dek: Faults, filter alerts and heating requests also become signals for automations.
body: Temperature targets can be set from 14–26°C for rooms and 20–55°C for domestic hot water. Each requested value is checked and read back from the controller before the interface shows it as accepted.

Kay also exposes fault signals, filter-replacement alerts, utility lockouts and operating requests. These can drive automations, while static information about installed capabilities starts disabled to avoid clutter. Ventilation-mode selection is separate work.

articles.title: Monthly electricity peaks come straight from the meter
articles.dek: Compatible Belgian DSMR 5B meters supply up to thirteen valid records, with timestamps.
body: The historical demand sensor exposes the peak readings already held in a Belgian meter’s monthly buffer. Invalid placeholders are left out, so the number of usable months depends on the meter.

TwicePower’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core also adds diagnostic information such as meter identifiers and switch or valve state. The historical readings do not change the current-month sensor’s reset timing or the separate DSMR Reader integration.

articles.title: Battery-only Envoys avoid a five-minute startup trap
articles.dek: A setup option skips solar-production requests when the gateway manages storage alone.
body: Adding Enphase batteries to a home with another brand of solar can leave the Envoy responsible only for storage. Asking that gateway for inverter production can stall setup long enough to exceed the five-minute limit.
The No solar option tells the integration to skip those requests and continue collecting battery data. It describes what the Envoy manages, not whether the home has solar panels.

Document enphase_envoy NO SOLAR mode

articles.title: Playback clients reject connections from web pages
articles.dek: The Python client library closes a route for a page on the local network to impersonate its server.
body: A browser page on the same network could open a connection to the client listener and act as a playback server. The listener rejects requests carrying the browser’s Origin header before the connection handler runs.

Ordinary server connections do not carry that header and continue as before. This is a change to the Python client library; it does not establish that every Sendspin speaker has received the protection.

articles.title: Your pet’s resting health indicators join the dashboard
articles.dek: The tracker service supplies the assessments; sensors appear only when health data is available.
body: Resting heart-rate and breathing-rate status, plus scratching status, draw on the health overview already received from Tractive. The integration adds no extra request to obtain them.

The sensors show unknown while the service is establishing a baseline or lacks enough data. F4llen’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core exposes the service’s assessments rather than making a diagnosis of its own.

articles.title: App authors get a timetable for discovery changes
articles.dek: Local hostname resolution stays intact as Supervisor retires its network-discovery relay.
body: Apps that browse for devices from the internal network should test with the multicast plugin disabled. Stefan Agner’s contributor guide explains how to check that dependency; apps using the host network, and those that only resolve .local names, need no change.
Supervisor 2026.12 stops installing the plugin on new systems. Version 2027.02 disables it on all installations but retains the option to turn it back on; removal follows in a later release.

articles.title: Artwork errors stop exposing music-service credentials
articles.dek: Warning messages conceal access tokens while keeping local addresses and paths useful for troubleshooting.
body: A failed cover-image download could write a Plex or Jellyfin access token into the log twice: once in the requested address and again in the error text. Marvin Schenkel filters the complete warning and its cached failure message before either is retained.

This closes a different exposure from October’s removal of Jellyfin credentials from library data. The correction covers image-download errors across providers, including credentials embedded directly in an address.

articles.title: Put night mode and speech enhancement into automations
articles.dek: Sonos options supplied by Music Assistant 2.11 become Home Assistant switches.
body: The switches for loudness, night mode and speech enhancement are enabled by default for supported speakers. Additional controls include the subwoofer and surround speakers, status light, touch controls and Trueplay.
These are speaker sound and hardware settings, separate from the queue’s Crossfade and Autoplay controls covered yesterday. Less common switches start disabled and can be enabled when needed.

articles.title: Idle touchscreens stop pressing their own buttons
articles.dek: Invalid reports from supported CST8xx controllers are filtered before they become a touch.
body: A tabletop music controller could pause or resume playback every minute or two without anyone touching it. An idle report was being interpreted as a press in the far corner of the display.

@Mattheinrichs’s first ESPHome contribution rejects those invalid reports while retaining real touches. A hardware check on a Makerfabs MaTouch display found no phantom presses during a six-minute capture with the correction applied to ESPHome 2026.10.
